france24fr.description: Un sommet de deux jours s'ouvre jeudi à Montréal entre l'Union européenne et la Canada. Objectif : étendre la coopération aux minerais stratégiques, au commerce numérique, à la recherche ou à la mobilité des jeunes, dans un contexte de tensions commerciales avec Donald Trump. Face aux réticences de plusieurs États membres, dont l’Allemagne, Bruxelles devrait toutefois renoncer à qualifier le Canada de "membre associé".

france24fr.title: En France, le Sénat vote l'imprescriptibilité des crimes sexuels commis sur les mineurs
france24fr.description: Les sénateurs ont largement approuvé mercredi l'imprescriptibilité des crimes sexuels commis sur les mineurs, une mesure inédite jusqu’ici réservée aux crimes contre l’humanité. Le texte doit encore être validé lors d’un vote solennel mardi puis en commission mixte paritaire.

france24fr.title: Les enjeux de la 3e édition du sommet Russie-Afrique
france24fr.description: Vladimir Poutine a accueilli ce mercredi une vingtaine de dirigeants africains pour la 3e édition du sommet Russie-Afrique. L'occasion de resserrer les liens avec un continent riche en minerais et en terres rares, dans un contexte de guerre avec l'Ukraine.

france24fr.title: Élections en Israël : pas de majorité en vue
france24fr.description:
On revient sur les résultats des élections législatives en Israël. Des élections très importantes, car ce sont les premières depuis les attaques du Hamas, le 7 octobre.
 
Ce soir, aucun des deux blocs n’obtient la majorité : ni celui de Benyamin Netanyahou, ni celui de Gadi Eisenkot.

france24fr.title: États-Unis : vent de rumeurs à l'approche des Midterms
france24fr.description: A l'approche des élections de mi-mandat, le 3 novembre aux Etats-Unis, les accusations de fraude tournent à plein régime tout comme les accusations mensongères visant certains candidats. Ainsi : des machines à voter de l'Illinois chercheraient à influencer le choix de l'électeur, ou le prétendant démocrate au Sénat dans le Texas James Talarico aurait par le passé abusé sexuellement d'un de ses élèves.

france24fr.title: Gabriel Attal prône une "primaire des démocrates" avant l'élection présidentielle en France
france24fr.description: Gabriel Attal, candidat à la présidentielle française, a proposé mercredi l'organisation d'une "primaire des démocrates" pour empêcher que le second tour oppose LFI au RN. L'accueil de cette idée est pour l'instant plutôt froid chez les partisans d'Édouard Philippe et Bruno Retailleau.

france24fr.title: Collision de trains en Espagne : que s'est-il passé ?
france24fr.description:
L’Espagne est en deuil après la collision de deux trains qui a fait au moins 68 morts dans le centre du pays. Alors que trois jours de deuil national ont été décrétés, les questions se posent sur les circonstances de cette catastrophe et les responsabilités éventuelles.
 
Benoît Pellistrandi, historien spécialiste de l’Espagne, revient sur le choc provoqué par ce drame.

france24fr.title: Alvin Hellerstein, le juge américain en charge de l'affaire Maduro, est mort à 92 ans
france24fr.description: Le juge fédéral américain Alvin Hellerstein, qui était notamment en charge de la procédure à l'encontre du président vénézuélien déchu Nicolas Maduro, est mort mercredi à l'âge de 92 ans. Lors d'une audience récente, il était apparu extrêmement fatigué, s'exprimant parfois avec difficulté.

france24fr.title: Guinée : Mamady Doumbouya, nouveau président de la Fédération de football
france24fr.description: 🇬🇳 ⚽En Guinée, à 34 ans, Mamady Doumbouya prend les commandes de la Feguifoot. Soutenu par plusieurs hommes d’affaires fortunés, il promet des investissements pour relancer le football guinéen.

france24fr.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : le public sera-t-il au rendez-vous ?
france24fr.description: 🇸🇳 Le Sénégal accueille le premier événement olympique organisé en Afrique. À quelques jours de l’ouverture des Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse Dakar 2026, une question se pose : le public sera-t-il au rendez-vous ? Reportage de Alexandrine Holognon.

france24fr.title: La gauche dénonce la tenue de manifestations "néofascistes" ce week-end à Paris
france24fr.description: La France insoumise et plusieurs voix de la gauche ont dénoncé mercredi la tenue de plusieurs événements "néofascistes" ce week-end à Paris. Parmi eux, une séance de dédicace, prévue vendredi, du militant autrichien d'extrême droite Martin Sellner, ou encore une manifestation prévue dimanche par le collectif Objectif remigration.

france24fr.title: Choc violent, "erreur humaine" : ce que l'on sait du drame ferroviaire qui endeuille encore l'Espagne
france24fr.description: Une collision mortelle survenue mercredi ​matin entre deux trains à grande vitesse près d'Urda, au sud de Madrid, endeuille de nouveau l'Espagne, neuf mois après une précédente catastrophe ferroviaire d'ampleur. Cette fois, la piste de l'"erreur humaine" est privilégiée. Voici ce que l'on en sait.

france24fr.title: Destructions des oliviers en Cisjordanie : quels impacts pour l'environnement
france24fr.description: Chaque année pendant la récolte des olives, des oliviers des Palestiniens de Cisjordanie occupée sont incendiés, arrachés ou endommagés par des colons israéliens et l'armée. Depuis 2023, environ 286 000 oliviers ont été détruits ou endommagés. Des destructions qui ont un impact considérable sur l'environnement, dans ce territoire très touché par le changement climatique.

france24fr.title: En fuyant le Brésil, Flavio Bolsonaro a-t-il condamné le bolsonarisme ?
france24fr.description: La décision de Flavio Bolsonaro de rejoindre les États-Unis deux jours après avoir perdu l'élection présidentielle contre Lula porte un coup dur à la réputation de la famille Bolsonaro, déjà entachée par les enquêtes judiciaires. Mais le Brésil n'est pas forcément prêt pour autant à tourner la page du bolsonarisme.

france24fr.title: Le changement climatique doit être déclaré «urgence sanitaire mondiale» (scientifiques)
france24fr.description: Le changement climatique constitue "la plus grande menace pour l'humanité". Dans son dixième rapport annuel, la revue médicale The Lancet Countdown appelle à reconnaître le changement climatique comme une «urgence sanitaire mondiale», alors que les phénomènes climatiques extrêmes se multiplient et que les conséquences sanitaires du réchauffement s'aggravent.

france24fr.title: Dolores Huerta, défenseuse des droits civiques et figure du syndicalisme aux États-Unis, est morte
france24fr.description: Dolores Huerta, syndicaliste qui avait cofondé le syndicat United Farm Workers, la principale organisation américaine de défense des travailleurs agricoles, dans les années 1960, est morte mercredi à l'âge de 96 ans.

france24fr.title: Au moins 50 000 personnes ont fui au Kenya en raison d’affrontements dans le sud de l'Éthiopie
france24fr.description: Quelque 50 000 personnes ont fui les récents affrontements qui opposent, depuis plusieurs jours dans le sud de l'Éthiopie, des forces armées des régions Somali et de l'Oromia, pour se réfugier au Kenya, a indiqué l'ONU mercredi.

zeit.description: Wenn das zweite Kind ganz anders ist als das erste, schwindet der Glaube an die eigenen Fähigkeiten. Und das ist eine der besten Erfahrungen, die Eltern machen können.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Der vergoldete Makel: wieso die Verklärung von ADHS und Autismus zur «Superkraft» gefährlich ist
nzz.description: Wer heute wahrgenommen werden will, muss einzigartig sein. Dabei deutet man selbst psychische Störungen positiv um. Eine Gesellschaft, die solche Selbstdarstellungen belohnt, verharmlost wirkliches Leiden.

nzz.title: Netanyahu braucht Partner. Doch kaum jemand will noch mit ihm regieren
nzz.description: Die Wahl in Israel hat keine klare Mehrheit gebracht. Ministerpräsident Benjamin Netanyahu könnte deshalb eine Regierung mit der Opposition bilden. Doch die Oppositionspolitiker haben viele Gründe, dem Ministerpräsidenten zu misstrauen.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Deutschland erhöht das Elterngeld – doch die bürokratischen Hürden für Familien bleiben bestehen
nzz.description: Statt Eltern immer neue Anreize zu setzen, sollte der Staat ihnen mehr Freiheit lassen und die Verwaltung vereinfachen. Damit wäre jungen Familien mehr geholfen als mit einer lange überfälligen Erhöhung.

nzz.title: In Lugano soll eine Strasse nach Giuliano Bignasca benannt werden – dagegen gibt es prominenten Widerstand
nzz.description: Lugano will den umstrittenen Lega-Gründer mit einer Strasse mitten im Zentrum ehren. Das sorgt für politischen Streit – und birgt einige Ironie.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Dreiergipfel in China: Die Welt wird sich Washington, Peking und Moskau nicht unterwerfen
nzz.description: Mitte November wollen sich die Präsidenten Putin, Xi und Trump in China zum Dreiergipfel treffen. Doch Europa sollte sich nicht zu sehr fürchten. Russland ist schwach, und China bleibt auf seine Handelspartner rund um den Globus angewiesen.

nzz.description: Nichts Neues unter der Sonne? Wer das glaubt, wird durch das neue Grossteleskop in Chile eines Besseren belehrt.

nzz.description: Der schwedische Bestsellerautor und Journalist begibt sich auf die Suche nach Traumata: Die Detektivarbeit, mit der ein Tag im Leben einer Familie rekonstruiert wird, ist eindrücklich.

nzz.title: Bei der Route du Rhum hat der französische Segler Jean Le Cam ein Rendez-vous mit der Vergangenheit
nzz.description: Nach zwanzig Jahren nimmt Jean Le Cam wieder am Atlantikrennen teil. Diesmal mit einer Fahrtenrennjacht alter Schule. Er freut sich auf «echte Seemannschaft».

nzz.title: Neuseeland hat den Fluss  Whanganui zur juristischen Person erklärt. Eine Reise entlang seiner Ufer

letemps.description:
Les Genevoises ont dominé, assez nettement, les doubles championnes de Belgique en titre du OH Louvain (5-1). Un succès qui leur permet de se replacer au classement, même si la suite du programme s’annonce autrement périlleuse

Le neuvième match aura été le bon! Les footballeuses du Servette FC Chênois Féminin tiennent la toute première victoire de l’histoire du club en Ligue des championnes.

letemps.title: Evoquant le destin de Matthew Perry, Netflix propose un documentaire digne et prudent
letemps.description:
Mary Robertson signe un triptyque sur les triomphes ainsi que le calvaire lent, et fatal, de l’acteur de «Friends». Un document sans les acteurs de la sitcom, mais nourri par des fidèles amis du comédien

Il y a certains amis, mais pas «les» amis. Le triptyque documentaire consacré à Matthew Perry, que Netflix a sorti mardi, repose sur de touchantes discussions avec la sœur de l’acteur disparu

letemps.title: Avant les élections de mi-mandat aux Etats-Unis, la Fed ne bouge pas ses taux
letemps.description:
La Réserve fédérale américaine laisse ses taux directeurs dans une fourchette de 3,75% à 4%. Elle ne voulait pas prendre de décision qui aurait été jugée politique. La Banque du Canada, elle, relève son taux

La Réserve fédérale américaine (Fed) a sans surprise opté mercredi pour le statu quo sur ses taux directeurs à quelques jours d’élections aux États-Unis largement centrées sur l’inflation

letemps.title: En vidéo – Pourquoi la Chine est-elle en colère contre Kylian Mbappé?
letemps.description:
C’est une vidéo de Kylian Mbappé qui semble innocente à nos yeux d’Occidentaux. Elle a pourtant provoqué la colère en Chine. Une affaire qui a coûté au footballeur français le départ de deux sponsors, ainsi que l’arrêt de la diffusion des matchs de la Liga. On vous explique en vidéo

C’est à cause de ces propos, «dictateur chinois», montés avec une image de Mao Tsé-toung que la Chine est en co

letemps.title: A Genève, un projet de loi ambitionne de redonner un visage humain au droit de la famille
letemps.description:
Après sept ans de travaux, la faîtière Avenir Familles et plusieurs partis politiques demandent la création d’un tribunal de protection de la famille. Objectif: remettre de l’ordre et du sens dans les nombreuses et douloureuses procédures de séparation

Parents contraints à devenir des adversaires lors des séparations, lenteurs extrêmes dans les procédures, enfances malmenées et paupérisation

letemps.title: Rente ou capital: l’inquiétant Röstigraben du deuxième pilier
letemps.description: OPINION. En Suisse, un Röstigraben apparaît lors du retrait du deuxième pilier. Les décisions différentes entre les Romands et les Alémaniques illustrent une chose: il existe une sorte de biais culturel alors que le choix de profiter d’une rente ou d’un capital devrait être dicté par un bilan économique personnel, écrit Soufiane Hamri, fondateur de la fintech genevoise de planification financière P

letemps.title: Dans le canton de Vaud, le bras de fer se poursuit entre les syndicats et le Conseil d’Etat
letemps.description:
La rencontre de mercredi n’a pas permis de trouver un terrain d’entente sur le budget 2027. La décision sur l’indexation des salaires, attendue le 4 novembre à la veille de la manifestation de la fonction publique, pourrait encore durcir le conflit

Sans surprise, le Conseil d’Etat vaudois maintient ses 100 millions de francs de coupes et les syndicats leur mobilisation du 5 novembre

spiegel.title: In den USA ist Ella Langley zurzeit erfolgreicher als Taylor Swift. Warum ist sie den Deutschen so egal?
spiegel.description: Popstar Ella Langley bricht in den USA Rekorde, hierzulande wird man nicht warm mit ihr. Woran liegt das?

spiegel.title: Sodbrennen/Reflux: Warum viele Menschen Magensäureblocker nehmen, obwohl sie es nicht bräuchten
spiegel.description: Bei Sodbrennen oder Reflux greifen Millionen Menschen in Deutschland regelmäßig zu Protonenpumpenhemmern. Dabei würden viele wohl gut ohne sie auskommen. Wie man sie richtig absetzt.

spiegel.title: Linkenpolitikerin Elif Eralp offenbart Angst vor Terrorsympathisanten
spiegel.description: Elif Eralp möchte Regierende Bürgermeisterin Berlins werden. Doch in einem internen Vermerk zeigt die Linkenpolitikerin, dass sie sich vor Terrorsympathisanten mit Kontakten zur Hamas fürchtet. Kann so jemand für die Sicherheit in der Hauptstadt verantwortlich sein? Die SPIEGEL-Titelstory.

spiegel.title: News: Elif Eralps Angst vor Hamas-Sympathisanten, Zugunglück in Spanien, VW-Quartalszahlen
spiegel.description: Elif Eralp will Berlin regieren und sieht sich bedroht. Das Bahnunglück in Spanien ist schrecklich – aber kein Grund, nicht in den Zug zu steigen. Und VW verkündet mal wieder miese Zahlen. Das ist die Lage am Donnerstagmorgen.

spiegel.title: Ist Tofu eine natürliche Proteinquelle – oder Hormonbombe? Der Check
spiegel.description: Sojaprodukte sollen angeblich Männerbrüste wachsen lassen, impotent machen und Brustkrebs fördern. Kann die eiweißreiche Hülsenfrucht wirklich den Hormonhaushalt stören? Das sagt der Ernährungswissenschaftler.

spiegel.title: Ralf Schumacher: Geplatzter Reifen auf Startbahn verhindert Flug nach Salzburg
spiegel.description: Mit Geschwindigkeit, Reifen und Notbremsen kennt sich Ex-Formel-1-Pilot Ralf Schumacher bestens aus. Nun lernte er all das aus einer ganz anderen Perspektive kennen: Sein Flug Richtung Salzburg musste annulliert werden.

spiegel.title: Iran-Konflikt: USA versuchen es mit Diplomatie – doch nach Midterms drohen neue Angriffe
spiegel.description: Die USA und Israel bereiten offenbar Militärschläge gegen Iran vor. Parallel laufen neue diplomatische Initiativen: Katar vermittelt und US-Vizepräsident Vance soll einen Brief geschrieben haben.

spiegel.title: Zugunglück in Spanien: Helfer auch nachts in Toledo im Einsatz – Ausschreitungen in Madrid
spiegel.description: Mit Kränen und Flutlicht arbeiten Einsatzkräfte an der Unglücksstelle in der spanischen Provinz Toledo, in den Trümmern der Züge werden weitere Opfer befürchtet. Vor dem Verkehrsministerium geraten rechte Demonstranten mit der Polizei aneinander.

spiegel.title: Hayden Panettiere: Polizei stuft Tod offiziell als Unfall ein
spiegel.description: Die Gerichtsmedizin hatte im Fall der verstorbenen Schauspielerin Hayden Panettiere von einer Überdosis gesprochen. Jetzt stellt die Polizei im US-Bundesstaat South Carolina ihre Ermittlungen ein.

spiegel.title: Kanada und EU: Plan von Ursula von der Leyen für Sonderstatus offenbar gescheitert
spiegel.description: Ursula von der Leyen hatte einen Sonderstatus für Kanada vorgeschlagen, als erstes »assoziiertes« Mitglied der EU. Nun ist der Entwurf der Abschlusserklärung des EU-Kanada-Gipfels durchgesickert. Darin fehlen entscheidende Wörter.

spiegel.title: Trump will sich nicht in Brasilien einmischen
spiegel.description: Der rechte Kandidat verliert die Präsidentschaftswahl in Brasilien. Donald Trump nennt sie »manipuliert« – will sich nun aber nicht mehr am Streit über die Wahl beteiligen.

spiegel.title: Haushaltsplan 2027: Italien plant Steuersenkungen und höhere Bankenabgaben
spiegel.description: Im Haushaltsplan für 2027 kündigt die Regierung Meloni Entlastungen für Selbstständige und mittlere Einkommen an. Auf Banken, Versicherungen, Energiekonzerne und auf die Glücksspielbranche kommen zusätzliche Abgaben zu.

spiegel.title: DFB-Pokal: Zweimal Olise – Bayern feiern 6:1-Kantersieg über Magdeburg
spiegel.description: 6:1 gewonnen, Kane geschont – und am Ende war Gegner Magdeburg sogar ein bisschen stolz. Mehr Selbstbewusstsein als die Bayern kann man im Pokal kaum tanken. Nun geht es in der Liga gegen den Rivalen aus Dortmund.

spiegel.title: Jemen: Uno meldet 280.000 Vertriebene durch anhaltende Kämpfe
spiegel.description: Die Kämpfe im Jemen haben laut der Uno derzeit 280.000 Menschen zur Flucht gezwungen. Gleichzeitig erschweren beschädigte Straßen die Versorgung der Vertriebenen mit lebenswichtigen Hilfsgütern.

spiegel.title: US-Notenbank: Analysten wetten schon auf die nächste Erhöhung der Zinsen
spiegel.description: Fed-Chef Kevin Warsh verkündet eine Zinspause, aber zwei seiner Gouverneure forderten angesichts der hohen Inflation schon dieses Mal eine Erhöhung. Haben die bevorstehenden Midterms doch eine Rolle gespielt?

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM: Fifa nimmt offenbar fünf Milliarden Dollar mit Ticketverkäufen ein
spiegel.description: Viele Spiele, hohe Preise: Die Fußball-WM in Nordamerika war ein Turnier der Superlative. Einem Bericht der »Times« zufolge sollen die Tickets der Fifa fünfmal höhere Einnahmen beschert haben als vier Jahre zuvor in Katar.

spiegel.title: Brasilien: Flávio Bolsonaro behauptet, Präsidentschaftswahl gewonnen zu haben
spiegel.description: Ein Verlierer, der es nicht wahrhaben will: Flávio Bolsonaro hat sich nach seiner Wahlpleite und Flucht geäußert. Und das nächste Ermittlungsverfahren wartet bereits in Brasilien.

spiegel.title: FC Bayern München: Vincent Kompany nach Hirnhautreizung aus Klinik entlassen
spiegel.description: Es geht aufwärts für Vincent Kompany: Der Bayern-Coach ist nach seinem Zusammenbruch nicht länger im Krankenhaus und schont sich zuhause weiter. Sportvorstand Max Eberl gab auch Auskunft über Kompanys Diagnose.

elpais.title: ¿Por qué chocaron los trenes? Tres fallos catastróficos que han costado 68 vidas
elpais.description: Se apuntan al menos tres problemas encadenados. Repasamos lo que sabemos del accidente y las principales incógnitas

elpais.title: Un error humano a las 8.36: la cadena de fallos y decisiones con las que el Gobierno explica la nueva tragedia en la línea Madrid-Sevilla
elpais.description: EL PAÍS accede a los audios de las comunicaciones entre los maquinistas de los trenes siniestrados y el centro de coordinación de Atocha, que les ordenó “marcha normal”

elpais.title: Yo viajaba en ese tren
elpais.description: Antonio Jiménez Barca, periodista de EL PAÍS, se encontraba en la cafetería del AVE en el momento en que impactó en el Iryo. Relata los primeros momentos de caos

elpais.title: Los audios del accidente|El controlador de Atocha, al maquinista del AVE: “Desconecte y vuelva a conectar. Reanude con marcha normal”
elpais.description: Los audios muestran el error del responsable de Atocha. La maquinista del Iryo avisó a cinco minutos de la tragedia de que estaba detenida y no podía arrancar el tren. Y nadie frenó al AVE

elpais.title: Los cabos por atar del siniestro de Urda en las investigaciones judicial y técnica
elpais.description: Las pesquisas se centran en las inconexas órdenes desde el centro de control de Adif al AVE e Iryo siniestrados, para la reanudación de la marcha con el sistema de seguridad LZB caído y con 35 años en operación, y la incapacidad del último para arrancar antes de la colisión

elpais.title: “Podríamos y deberíamos hacer más”: los expertos piden invertir en el mantenimiento de la alta velocidad
elpais.description: España destina a conservar la red ferroviaria menos que otros países europeos, según datos de la Comisión Europea y de los ingenieros de caminos

elpais.title: Las líneas de alta velocidad española vuelven a teñirse de sangre
elpais.description: Al menos 68 personas han perdido la vida en una nueva colisión de trenes en la línea Madrid-Sevilla. Expertos consultados plantean: “¿Si se permite que el error de un solo hombre provoque decenas de víctimas, es un fallo del hombre o del sistema?"

elpais.title: Peregrinaje por pueblos y llamadas a los hospitales para encontrar a los desaparecidos: “Saben que está vivo, pero no dónde”
elpais.description: En el pabellón habilitado para atender a los afectados, la incertidumbre se mezcla con el miedo mientras las familias intentan reconstruir el paradero de quienes viajaban en los trenes accidentados

elpais.title: La tragedia da un vuelco al guion de la campaña
elpais.description: El Gobierno está en ‘shock’ por un accidente que se le sitúa en el peor escenario político posible en plena contienda electoral; Sánchez mantiene de momento la confianza en Puente. Feijóo adopta un tono institucional con un PP muy a la contra, mientras el Frente Amplio pide responsabilidades políticas y Vox señala a Sánchez

elpais.title: Empieza otra campaña electoral
elpais.description: Después de los tres días de luto, va a ser muy difícil para el PSOE recuperar la campaña en positivo y muy fácil para el PP hablar de la ‘España del caos’

elpais.title: Antonio, pasajero del AVE, busca a su amigo Alberto: “Hasta que no aparezca, no me voy”
elpais.description: Los supervivientes y los vecinos de Urda se vuelcan en las tareas de rescate y en la búsqueda de los desaparecidos tras uno de los accidentes ferroviarios más graves de España

elpais.title: Catástrofes inasumibles
elpais.description: El segundo choque mortal de dos trenes de alta velocidad en menos de un año es un golpe a la confianza de los ciudadanos en el Estado

elpais.title: Se acabó la campaña
elpais.description: Mientras se determina si el fallo fue estructural o humano, a muchos no se nos quitará el miedo fundado a coger unos trenes que llevan más de 100 muertos en menos de un año

elpais.title: El regreso de C. Tangana a la música con el grupo de rap que lo cambió todo y al que tildaron de pijo
elpais.description: En Agorazein, el colectivo de hip hop del que salió El Madrileño y que vuelve para solo cuatro conciertos en Movistar Arena, cabe la historia de cómo el rap que los oyentes llamaron “blandito” se convirtió en la música popular de hoy

elpais.title: Susi Sánchez, actriz: “Vivimos en un mundo muy difícil, muy retorcido, y a veces pierdo el contacto conmigo y necesito preservarme”
elpais.description: La ganadora de dos premios Goya y un premio Max actúa en ‘El mal hijo’, ópera prima como director del intérprete Jaime Lorente

elpais.title: Palomo cumple 10 años en la moda: “Karl Lagerfeld no fue muy amable conmigo. Beyoncé, sí”
elpais.description: Quería ser una gran figura de la moda, pero no un personaje y, una década después, ha conseguido las dos cosas. Para celebrar su aniversario, repasa sus cinco momentos clave

elpais.title: Bar Gros, la taberna de barrio que arrasa en el centro de Barcelona:“Por 35 euros sales con el estómago lleno”
elpais.description: Este nevo riunfa con su filosofía de ‘cuanto más mejor’ en pleno corazón de la ciudad condal. “Somos gente sencilla a la que le gusta la cocina sencilla”

elpais.title: Lo del doctor Cabrera en ‘Horizonte’
elpais.description: El habitual colaborador de programas de televisión de Telecinco, Cuatro y Antena 3 lanza intervenciones fuera de lugar ante las risas de tertulianos y la agitación de las redes sociales

republika.title: Scioperi del 30 ottobre: l’Italia si ferma, ecco i dettagli e i motivi della protesta
republika.description: Nella giornata dello stop di USB e Cobas torneranno in piazza anche gli studenti, in tutte le principali città

republika.title: La Juve affonda e Spalletti ammette: “Facciamo fatica a capire il calcio di oggi”
republika.description: Le analisi sono già cominciate e impietosamente si è arrivati a una prima conclusione: la Juve non regge sul piano agonistico.

republika.title: Flat tax fino a 100mila euro. Pagano assicurazioni e giochi. Nulla per le tredicesime
republika.description: Per il ceto medio sgravio massimo di 500 euro all’anno sull’Irpef. Fondi alla salute lontani dai bisogni delle Regioni. Coperture: 700 milioni dai big energetici

republika.title: Manovra, Meloni avvisa gli alleati: “Niente errori in Parlamento”. Ultime scintille sulle tasse
republika.description: In cdm tensione su flat tax e contributo degli istituti di credito. Lo sfogo di Schillaci: “Mettiamo fondi non incassati”. Meloni, stop a Salvini su Kiev

republika.title: Manovra, Boccia: “Solo spot e propaganda, chi arriverà dopo troverà macerie”
republika.description: Il presidente dei senatori del Pd: “Misure disomogenee e solito imbroglio sulla sanità. L’anno prossimo come coprirà i bonus?”

republika.title: “Quella gip è schierata con Gaza” il fango della destra su Landoni
republika.description: Sotto accusa per un appello pro Palestina di un anno fa Ma la stessa petizione porta la firma della pm che ha chiesto il carcere per Siher

republika.title: Ecco perché Siher è stato liberato: i cinque capitoli che smontano le accuse della procura
republika.description: Per la gip Tiziana Landoni “nessun piano eversivo, la sua era solo disobbedienza civile”

republika.title: Scontri del 17 ottobre, l’allarme dell’intelligence ignorato dal Viminale
republika.description: I Servizi avevano segnalato i disordini che poi si sono verificati. L’ombra di una regia unica dietro i volantini che hanno chiamato le piazze

republika.title: Youssef Siher e gli applausi all’uscita da San Vittore: “Ora voglio stare in famiglia”
republika.description: «È molto contento e ha bisogno di riposo, stare a San Vittore non è una passeggiata specie per chi che non ci doveva stare dall’inizio» ha detto una dei suoi avvocati, Yasmina Abu Sharar

republika.title: Netanyahu è di nuovo primo ma non ha la maggioranza. Prende corpo l’idea di un governo di unità nazionale
republika.description: La coalizione del premier israeliano incassa 53 seggi contro i 48 dell’opposizione. Exploit dei palestinesi. Cresce l’attesa per le scelte del presidente Herzog

republika.title: Il leader del partito palestinese: “La pace e stop alle demolizioni delle case. Se Eisenkot accetta, lo sosteniamo”
republika.description: Sami Abu Shehadeh: “Toglieremo alla destra la presidenza della Knesset, votando con l’opposizione: a dimostrazione che siano pronti all’alleanza”

republika.title: Le metamorfosi di Bibi, “il mago” delle alleanze per restare al potere
republika.description: Il premier ha fatto leva sulla paura per sfilare voti agli alleati di destra Smotrich e Ben Gvir: così ha limitato la perdita di consenso ed è rimasto al centro dell’agone. Ora nulla gli impedisce di rimanere al governo

republika.title: A Gaza la notte insonne davanti alla tv per seguire le elezioni: “Al risveglio la delusione”
republika.description: Generatori e telefoni: la popolazione stremata si è arrangiata per lo spoglio. “Sembrava Netanyahu fosse fuori, così non cambia nulla”

republika.title: Gitai “Non tutto è perduto, serve un progetto comune per andare oltre l’odio”
republika.description: Il regista: “I cittadini arabi di Israele hanno capito che possono battersi per cambiare il Paese insieme alle forze progressiste”

republika.title: L’ex ministra, turisti e giovani tra le vittime: “Come l’apocalisse”
republika.description: Le operazioni di soccorso andate avanti senza sosta per tutta la notte, si è scavato anche con l’aiuto dei droni. Il sacerdote: “Ho dato l’estrema unzione a due ragazzi, sono sconvolto”

republika.title: Due stragi in un anno sulla stessa linea. Sanchez sotto accusa, tre giorni di lutto
republika.description: Lo schianto irrompe nella corsa alle elezioni del 29 novembre: si accende il confronto su sicurezza e manutenzione dei trasporti

republika.title: Fenomeno Ossoff ad Atlanta, la benedizione di Obama può valere la Casa Bianca
republika.description: L’ex presidente è volato ieri nella città di Martin Luther King per sostenere il giovane senatore che cerca la riconferma. Il comizio sembra un passaggio del testimone a quello che potrebbe diventare il suo erede politico

republika.title: Djokovic da traditore a eroe, Serbia pronta a riaccoglierlo
republika.description: Il campione, schierato con gli studenti anti-Vucic, era finito nella lista nera delle tv di Stato e aveva lasciato il Paese. Ora valuta il ritorno

nyt.title: Cabinet Officials on the Campaign Trail? Ethics Experts Say Some Are Breaking the Law.
nyt.description: As Trump officials stump for Republican candidates facing difficult races, ethics experts say they are being lax about complying with the Hatch Act, a federal anti-corruption law.

nyt.title: As Trump Faces Down the Midterms, a Grim Mood Takes Over the White House
nyt.description: The White House has been rocked by turnover and anxiety over the midterms. The president, who is tightening his inner circle, has lashed out at critics, held meandering rallies and feasted on a diet of news clips and “A.I. slop,” as one aide put it.

nyt.title: Inside Democrats’ Secret Effort to Stack Alaska’s Midterm Ballot With Another Dan Sullivan
nyt.description: Operatives aligned with Mary Peltola, the Democratic nominee for Senate, spent months recruiting candidates to peel votes from Senator Dan Sullivan, the Republican.

nyt.title: In Michigan, El-Sayed Faces Heat From Former Primary Rival as Election Nears
nyt.description: Representative Haley Stevens has been less than enthusiastic about Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, injecting late intraparty tensions into a race that could decide Senate control.

nyt.title: Judge Rejects Trump Officials’ Bid to Set Aside California Ballots
nyt.description: The judge ruled that no immediate action was necessary, dealing another setback to the administration as it moves to target voting by noncitizens.

nyt.title: Flávio Bolsonaro Lands in Miami After Fleeing Brazil
nyt.description: Mr. Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday’s presidential election, fled Brazil for the United States via Argentina after the police canceled his passport in relation to an investigation.

nyt.title: How André Janones Helped Turbocharge Lula’s Comeback in Brazil’s Election
nyt.description: With street talk and tactics from the far-right’s playbook, André Janones used a WhatsApp channel to help organize millions of Brazilians online.

nyt.title: Weil Gotshal, Once a Legal Powerhouse, Plans to Dissolve
nyt.description: The prominent law firm has been rocked by an exodus of high-profile lawyers, a failed succession plan and a scuttled deal to merge with a rival firm.

nyt.title: A Ukrainian City in the Kill Zone Relishes a Moment of Peace
nyt.description: A rare localized peace deal announced by the first lady, Melania Trump, offered a brief respite for Kherson, where Russian drones and artillery have long terrorized civilians.

nyt.title: Spain Train Crash Kills at Least 68
nyt.description: The accident, the second in less than a year on the same busy rail line, was one of the deadliest in the country’s history.

nyt.title: Is There a ‘Safest Seat’ in a Train Crash? Experts Say It’s Not So Simple.
nyt.description: After a high-speed collision near Toledo, Spain, killed at least 68 people, rail safety experts said the rough consensus that it is best to sit in the middle of a train has its limits.

nyt.title: Israel’s Parties Gird for Wrangling to Form a Government, With No Clear Path
nyt.description: Votes are still being counted, but it appears that neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing coalition nor the opposition alliance headed by Gadi Eisenkot will have a majority.

nyt.title: Surprise Showing by Arab Parties in Israeli Vote Puts Them in Spotlight
nyt.description: The Arab parties have long been kept on the political sidelines. But stunning turnout by their supporters makes the Arab minority an Israeli political reality that cannot be ignored.

nyt.title: Vance Proposes Restarting Peace Talks in Outreach to Iranian Official
nyt.description: In his letter, the vice president suggested an immediate resumption of comprehensive talks, including about Iran’s nuclear program.

nyt.title: Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas, Who Helped End One-Party Rule in Mexico, Dies at 92
nyt.description: Mr. Cárdenas, the only son of a Mexican president, never won the office but became a leading figure in the country’s democratic transformation.

nyt.title: She Was Arrested After Leaving Her Kids for Days. It Sparked a Debate.
nyt.description: A Florida sheriff’s office arrested a mother who had left her children home alone for days to go on a work trip, reigniting the debate over when parents act irresponsibly.

nyt.title: What Does the Cheesecake Factory’s Designer Think of Obama and Trump’s Jabs at His Décor?
nyt.description: Long before its baroque décor and class identity became midterm talking points, this durable restaurant chain survived some withering critiques.

nyt.title: Europe Is on Edge, and It’s Not Going to End
nyt.description: The protests roiling the continent express feelings of generational futility.

npr.title: Brazilian political drama unfolds as defeated Flavio Bolsonaro arrives in Miami
npr.description: Defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his family have arrived in the U.S. after Brazilian authorities ordered him to surrender his passport. He is facing multiple investigations in Brazil.

npr.title: Israel's election too close to call. And, the Ebola outbreak reaches grim milestone
npr.description: Israeli voters turned out in record numbers, and the results remain too close to call. And, more than 10,000 people have been infected with Ebola since the outbreak was first declared in May.

npr.title: Dozens are dead in a high-speed train crash in Spain
npr.description: The toll is rising after a high-speed train between slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped south of Madrid, derailing two cars. It was Spain's second major train accident this year.

npr.title: Trump's relationship with Putin comes under fire ahead of the midterms
npr.description: President Trump's relationship with Russia's Vladimir Putin is under scrutiny again as the president makes deals with Moscow ahead of the midterms.

npr.title: Partial results from Israel's contentious election show no clear winner
npr.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc was leading opposition rival Gadi Eisenkot. Arab parties had a strong showing, and a key question now is whether Eisenkot's bloc will consider forming a coalition with them.

npr.title: Ex-Israeli diplomat calls opposition's refusal to work with Arab parties 'reckless'
npr.description: Why a stronger showing for Arab parties may not translate into political power in Israel.

npr.title: A U.S. cruise ship ends voyage due to fuel costs and passengers lose their homes
npr.description: The Odyssey set sail two years ago on a three-year voyage to the seven continents marketed as combining long-term living at sea with global travel.

npr.title: Flávio Bolsonaro arrives in Florida after fleeing Brazil

phys-org.title: End of COVID-era SNAP emergency food assistance linked to increased child maltreatment rates
phys-org.description: A new study has found that in U.S. counties that ended COVID-19 pandemic-era Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) Emergency Allotments, child maltreatment rates went up. The findings from the study in the American Journal of Preventive Medicine suggest that changes to food assistance programs have consequences that extend beyond food security and also affect child and family well-being.

phys-org.title: Optimistic climate futures for local communities in the UK imagined in a new report
phys-org.description: A new report co-authored by researchers from the University of York and WWF highlights how local communities across the U.K. imagine positive, sustainable, and resilient futures for the places where they live and work.

phys-org.title: How the Indian Ocean is linked to Europe's early-winter rain and storms
phys-org.description: When we think about Europe's winter weather, the Indian Ocean is probably not the first place we look. We might picture Atlantic storms, cold air arriving from the north or rain sweeping across the Mediterranean. In my research, however, I look at how these familiar weather systems fit into a much larger climate system. My colleagues and I asked whether an ocean thousands of kilometers away could leave a detectable signature on Europe's early winter.

phys-org.title: The phantom lighthouse: New research explains one of Australia's strangest illusions
phys-org.description: There are two lighthouses on Lady Elliot Island, at the southernmost tip of Australia's Great Barrier Reef. The first was built in 1873, but was decommissioned in 1995 when the second took over the job of warning ships off the reef. Visitors to the island, however, regularly report seeing signs of a third lighthouse. At night the beams of a nonexistent phantom lighthouse are seen far off, shining on the horizon.

phys-org.title: Ultrathin metal layer boosts spin-related signals, opening a door to ultralow-power electronics
phys-org.description: Researchers at Kyushu University have found that an ultrathin layer of iridium manganese (IrMn) can improve two spin-related signals in a structure made of a magnetic insulator and a platinum film. By examining how spin currents are generated and absorbed, the team gained insights into how the intermediate layer improves spin transfer. The findings could inform the development of ultralow-power devices for computing and energy harvesting.

phys-org.title: Atomic magnetism reveals why iron, but not chromium, can produce ammonia using sunlight
phys-org.description: Two nearly identical materials have completely different chemical behavior. Research teams at the University of Vienna and TU Wien studied catalysts that use the energy of sunlight to produce ammonia. Surprisingly, when the three iron atoms that form tiny triangles in these catalysts are replaced by chromium atoms, the chemical reaction no longer takes place.

phys-org.title: Macromolecular crowding could help build artificial cell systems
phys-org.description: Macromolecular crowding can serve as a design tool for controlling the formation and organization of synthetic DNA droplets, a study from Science Tokyo reveals. Researchers investigated this strategy using DNA nanostars and polymeric crowding agents to mimic the crowded cellular environment. They found that crowding promoted droplet formation and enabled control over droplet size, interactions and organization. The findings could support the development of programmable artificial cell systems.

phys-org.title: Molecular architecture determines tomato plant resistance to its main pest
phys-org.description: An international study investigating why wild tomatoes are more resistant to the tomato leafminer (Phthorimaea absoluta) than cultivated varieties revealed that the secret lies in the spatial structure of a plant defense molecule. The researchers mapped the biochemical origin of this difference and demonstrated that altering four amino acids in a single enzyme is sufficient to alter the structure of the substance and increase its toxicity against the pest. phys-org.title: Explaining the difference between brittle and ductile behavior in polymer glasses
phys-org.description: Glasses are (mostly) brittle, metals can be ductile (plastic), and liquids flow easily. Polymers are interesting because they exhibit all three types of behavior, depending on their chemical nature, temperature, and deformation rate. If polymers are not able to crystallize, their low-temperature state is glassy, and they are hard and transparent. One example is poly(methylmethacrylate) [PMMA], which has been used as an artificial glass since the early 20th century.

phys-org.title: Q&A: Decoding the cell—a conversation with a computational biologist
phys-org.description: Computational biologist Christina Leslie, Ph.D., has spent nearly two decades at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSK) building computational tools that help make sense of some of the most complex data in biology.

phys-org.title: Chornobyl dog population shows genetic signatures of directional selection
phys-org.description: The latest research on the wild population of dogs in Chornobyl reveals that the genetic differences between these dogs and other similarly isolated dog populations are likely evidence of directional selection, not mutation. The work suggests a potential association between genetic selection and environmental variables and could advance understanding of local adaptation and genomic resilience in contaminated environments. The study appears in Genes.

phys-org.title: Could next-gen artificial intelligence help map out future space outposts?
phys-org.description: Planning a successful trip can be challenging, especially when your destination is in outer space. Even before liftoff, space missions require extraordinary amounts of scientific preparation and data analysis to succeed, which can take years to complete. However, as space agencies race to establish a permanent presence on the moon, using artificial intelligence to combine such information into a single system could make mission planning much more efficient.

phys-org.title: Same radical, different paths: X-ray snapshots reveal how neighboring molecules shape its movement
phys-org.description: Chemical reactions have their own "impatient molecules." Unable to stay still even for a moment, they latch onto other molecules indiscriminately. Researchers have now found that even these molecules change where they "sit" and how far they roam depending on who their neighbors are. The findings are expected to help scientists make better medicines and materials by directing reactions only to the desired sites.

phys-org.title: Schools increasingly affected by poor air quality as wildfire smoke becomes more common
phys-org.description: American children are increasingly exposed to air pollution as wildfire smoke becomes more common, and some schools and child care centers struggle to keep indoor breathing conditions clean, a new national study shows.

phys-org.title: Medieval ghost stories featured rotten flesh, the walking dead and spoon‑stealing spirits
phys-org.description: Stories of wandering spirits and the restless dead were common in the Middle Ages. These ghostly encounters were recorded in a wide variety of medieval literature.

phys-org.title: Rarely seen deep-sea barreleye fish filmed in 4K
phys-org.description: During a recent expedition aboard the research vessel David Packard, MBARI scientists encountered a rarely seen barreleye fish (Macropinna microstoma). This sighting is MBARI's 11th observation of this unique deep-sea fish with a transparent head.

phys-org.title: Drones could help weather forecasters more accurately predict winter storms
phys-org.description: Weather drones are being tested to help update forecasts of extreme weather more quickly, and could help us prepare earlier for upcoming winter storms.

phys-org.title: Controlling where gibberellin acts reveals how the plant hormone coordinates root growth
phys-org.description: Plant hormones influence growth and development by acting on specific cells and tissues. However, determining precisely where and when a hormone needs to act has been challenging because conventional hormone treatment generally activates signaling throughout the plant.

Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

proj-syn.title: A Tale of Two Chinas
proj-syn.description: China’s economy is deeply unbalanced, with a battered real-estate sector, weak consumption, and stark regional disparities coexisting with dynamic tech and export sectors. But provided that political stability is maintained, China could continue to be a global powerhouse even as hundreds of millions of its citizens remain poor.

proj-syn.title: Sino–American Stability?
proj-syn.description: Delegates at the Bund Summit in Shanghai largely agreed that the US-China relationship could be entering a new, less contentious chapter, although many were more interested in what the post-Trump era will mean for Sino-American ties. But perhaps the most heartening sign for the future was the honest exchange of views.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Winter of Discontent
proj-syn.description: Although it is true that European integration has always been forged through crisis, the continent’s postwar story was largely one of incremental responses to relatively manageable challenges. Today, the European Union is facing multiple, interrelated problems that challenge its very raison d’être.

proj-syn.title: How Students Dethroned Serbia’s Strongman
proj-syn.description: Following the ouster of Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán after 16 years in power earlier this year, the world has once again witnessed the merits of “old-school” campaigning. In toppling their own country's strongman, Serbia's new student-led opposition offers important lessons for those defending democracy elsewhere.

proj-syn.title: What a US-China AI Safety Channel Needs
proj-syn.description: Addressing AI safety risks depends on close collaboration between the two leading AI powers, and the establishment of an incident-reporting channel is just a small step in this direction. But success will require that the US and Chinese governments actually understand what is happening under their own noses.

proj-syn.title: The Authoritarian Logic of Selective Privacy
proj-syn.description: Around the world, governments are increasingly deciding who gets privacy and who is denied it, a double standard that turns a fundamental democratic right into a privilege. US President Donald Trump’s administration is a prime example, shielding ICE agents from scrutiny while expanding surveillance of immigrants and protesters.

proj-syn.title: Brazil’s Chapter in the Anti-Authoritarian Playbook
proj-syn.description: Brazil’s renewed democratic confidence must now be matched by institutional and structural reforms and a willingness to build coalitions beyond the left. Recent democratic outcomes in Hungary and Serbia offer useful lessons.

proj-syn.title: Another Crash Landing for Brazil’s Economy?
proj-syn.description: Brazil’s floating exchange rate, high foreign-exchange reserves, strong commodity exports, and debt denominated predominantly in its own currency reduce its exposure to a balance-of-payments crisis. Nonetheless, continued fiscal deterioration under President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will carry high domestic costs.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Make-or-Break Moment Has Arrived
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump has not only abandoned Ukraine and America’s European allies, but has increasingly sided with Russian President Vladimir Putin. To preserve their sovereignty, Europeans must remain united in the face of outside pressure, which in turn requires managing political threats from within their borders.

proj-syn.title: Middle Powers Can Lead on AI Safety
proj-syn.description: With the United States showing no interest in regulating AI, middle powers have an opportunity to take the lead on governance. By banding together, these countries could condition market access on meeting a common set of safety requirements and explore joint investment in technical capacity.

proj-syn.title: Lula Killed the Donroe Doctrine
proj-syn.description: In attempting to disentangle the United States from the rest of the world and retreat into a seemingly controllable hemispheric stronghold, Donald Trump's Latin America strategy had fared better than the rest of his foreign policy. But following a defeat for the far right in Brazil, his project now looks dead in the water.

proj-syn.title: The Wrong Way to Compare Economic Size
proj-syn.description: At the European Central Bank’s annual research conference, Paul Krugman concluded that, when it comes to “weaponized interdependence,” the EU is more powerful than both the US and China. But his reliance on PPP-adjusted GDP as a way to smooth out the volatility of nominal exchange rates ignores the even greater swings in PPP data.

proj-syn.title: Public Control for a Purposeful Economy
proj-syn.description: As more governments recognize the need for greater public control over economic outcomes, they must be careful to define the concept well. What ultimately matters is not ownership, but the state’s capacity to steer economic activity toward strategic objectives in the service of the common good.

proj-syn.title: Rethinking Sustainable Livelihoods From the Ground Up
proj-syn.description: In regions where economic activity has long revolved around fossil-fuel extraction, ensuring a just transition requires developing alternative livelihoods that account for each community’s specific needs. Regional endowment funds could be a useful vehicle for funding these local initiatives.

proj-syn.title: The Specter of an AI-Driven Slowdown
proj-syn.description: The rush to finance AI infrastructure is driving up borrowing costs just as governments grapple with mounting debt and persistent fiscal deficits. If the AI investment boom falters, falling valuations could choke off financing, with little room for fiscal and monetary policy to cushion the economic shock.

proj-syn.title: Is a Chinese Implosion Looming?
proj-syn.description: If current trends continue, the Chinese state will find itself exposed to a political succession crisis, a weakening economy, and a lack of resources to exercise power domestically and project it externally. It would be a perfect storm, with far-reaching global repercussions.

This is true of the global trading system, which has proven surprisingly resilient in recent years, and of the European economy, which might not have a tech giant to rival those in the US or China, but remains a global trade powerhouse and a leader in science and research. proj-syn.description: Civil-society oversight is the cheapest insurance in sovereign finance, because it enables independent scrutiny long before a default. But given that a borrowing government will never volunteer to fund the people who audit it, global decision-makers must do so using agreements for stolen-asset recovery and sovereign-debt treatments.

crunchbase.title: The Crunchbase Tech Layoffs Tracker
crunchbase.description: Over 127,000 workers at U.S.-based tech companies were laid off in mass job cuts in 2025, per a Crunchbase News tally, and the layoffs have continued into 2026. See the latest companies to cut roles.

crunchbase.title: Exclusive: Numeracle Raises $28M To Keep Legitimate Business Calls From Spam Label
crunchbase.description: Numeracle, a McLean, Virginia-based company that verifies businesses and links their identities to the phone numbers they use to contact customers, has raised $28 million from Edison Partners to help businesses whose calls are incorrectly labeled as spam or blocked by phone carriers.

crunchbase.title: The Invisible Graph: How Companies Grow Revenue And Still Lose Value
crunchbase.description: Revenue growth does not guarantee a larger exit, as declining valuation multiples can outweigh operating gains and reduce enterprise value. Guest author Itay Sagie suggests that founders and boards should track valuation alongside financial performance, model the effects of delaying a sale, and begin M&A preparation while the business is strong and buyer interest is favorable.

crunchbase.title: From Monk To Startups: One Founder’s Unusual Path To Building Government Software
crunchbase.description: After living as a monk while managing Graves’ disease, a former Facebook engineer left Big Tech to pursue meaningful work, eventually founding government software startup FSH Technologies which aims to improve processes such as school food services and public records management through the use of artificial intelligence.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data Shows Q3 Robotics Startup Funding Jumps 185% As US And China Lead Physical AI Push
crunchbase.description: Venture funding to robotics startups has soared in 2026, with the bulk of investment going to companies based in China and the U.S., Crunchbase data shows. All told, global venture funding to robotics startups totaled $9.9 billion in Q3, more than double the $4.3 billion invested in Q3 2025, per Crunchbase data.

crunchbase.title: Your AI Agents Need A Chief Operating Officer, Too
crunchbase.description: Scaling AI agents requires treating them like employees in regulated roles, with written rules, clearly defined responsibilities and a named human manager accountable for their performance. Guest author Rick Folgmann, COO at Get Covered, tells companies they should start with tasks governed by established rules, adjust autonomy to each workflow’s risks, and regularly review results before expanding agents’ authority.

crunchbase.title: Some Observations About Anthropic’s IPO Filing
crunchbase.description: In an S-1 filing today preceding what could be the largest IPO ever, Anthropic laid out extensive new details about its earnings, growth, key stakeholders and the risks it faces going forward. Clocking in at 335 pages, the document wasn’t exactly light reading. However, in a preliminary once-over, we highlight some of the more intriguing disclosures.

crunchbase.title: When Traction Becomes Personal Exposure: What The Joonko Guilty Plea Means For Founders
crunchbase.description: False claims about customers, revenue and AI capabilities can expose founders to personal securities-fraud liability, with D&O insurance offering limited protection against established misconduct. Guest author Kyle Jeziorski of Founder Shield shares three policy provisions that need close attention from founders.

crunchbase.title: California Startups Have Raised More So Far In 2026 Than The Entire US Ever Has In A Single Year
crunchbase.description: California companies have scooped up more than three-fourths of all U.S. startup funding this year. That, per Crunchbase data, is an apparent record share. And keep in mind: This year still has a couple months left.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI Drives A Varied Lineup Of Large Financings
crunchbase.description: It was another interesting week for AI-related startup funding, with a number of large rounds and quirky companies. The largest financings went to Tenstorrent, a developer of AI processors and systems, and AI lab Flapping Airplanes. The quirkiest round, meanwhile, was undoubtedly a $200 million financing for Warhound, which wants to breed elite military dogs. A number of big rounds in areas including biotech, space tech and physical AI rounded out the list.
